description: Initial investment-management workflow set for independent team scoring and reconciliation.

steps.name: Collect trade records
steps.description: Collect executed trade records from the order management system and broker confirmations.
steps.evidence: High-volume structured retrieval with stable source fields.

steps.name: Match trade fields
steps.description: Compare security, side, quantity, price, currency, trade date, settlement date, and account across the two records.
steps.evidence: Deterministic field comparison is auditable and exception-friendly.

steps.name: Investigate unmatched trade
steps.description: Review an unmatched or partially matched trade, contact the broker or trader, and determine the cause of the discrepancy.
steps.evidence: Repeated exceptions need better data and escalation design before automation.

steps.name: Release settlement exception
steps.description: Approve or reject the proposed correction and record the evidence before settlement instructions proceed.
steps.evidence: High-control approval depends on accountable operations judgment.

steps.name: Load positions and limits
steps.description: Load end-of-day positions, look-through exposures, and approved mandate limits for each portfolio.
steps.evidence: Scheduled structured data collection with repeatable controls.

steps.name: Calculate exposures
steps.description: Calculate issuer, sector, country, currency, and asset-class exposures against the configured limits.
steps.evidence: Rule-based computation is highly suitable if limit configuration is governed.

steps.name: Classify breach
steps.description: Determine whether an exception is a genuine breach, a data-timing issue, or an approved temporary tolerance.
steps.evidence: Exception taxonomy and data lineage should be standardized before agentic handling.

steps.name: Escalate confirmed breach
steps.description: Notify the portfolio manager and compliance officer, document the breach, and track remediation to closure.
steps.evidence: Escalation accountability and materiality decisions remain human-led.

steps.name: Receive breach alert
steps.description: Receive an alert identifying a possible investment guideline or client mandate breach.
steps.evidence: Alert intake and routing are structured and time-sensitive.

steps.name: Reconstruct portfolio state
steps.description: Reconstruct holdings, transactions, prices, cash, and applicable mandate rules at the time of the suspected breach.
steps.evidence: Data lineage and time-versioned rules must be improved before reliable automation.

steps.name: Assess cause and materiality
steps.description: Determine whether the event was caused by trading, market movement, data error, or client instruction and assess materiality.
steps.evidence: Contextual fiduciary and compliance judgment is central.

steps.name: Prepare breach report
steps.description: Prepare the documented breach analysis, corrective action, client communication recommendation, and approval record.
steps.evidence: Drafting can be assisted, but approval and workflow controls need redesign.

steps.name: Collect client information
steps.description: Collect identity, financial circumstances, investment objectives, experience, restrictions, and risk information from the client.
steps.evidence: Structured intake and completeness checks can be automated with consent controls.

steps.name: Validate evidence
steps.description: Validate identity, source documents, financial evidence, and required disclosures for completeness and consistency.
steps.evidence: Document and exception handling should be standardized before automation.

steps.name: Assess suitability
steps.description: Assess whether the proposed investment approach is suitable for the client's objectives, capacity for loss, and constraints.
steps.evidence: Client-specific judgment and duty of care cannot be delegated to a black box.

steps.name: Approve onboarding
steps.description: Review the suitability rationale and approve the client relationship or request clarification and remediation.
steps.evidence: Accountable approval should remain with an appropriately authorized professional.

steps.name: Collect performance inputs
steps.description: Collect portfolio returns, benchmark data, holdings, cash flows, fees, and commentary inputs for the reporting period.
steps.evidence: Recurring structured data assembly with clear period boundaries.

steps.name: Calculate and reconcile returns
steps.description: Calculate time-weighted and money-weighted returns where applicable and reconcile them to the performance system.
steps.evidence: Calculation and reconciliation rules are repeatable and testable.

steps.name: Investigate performance variance
steps.description: Investigate material differences from benchmark or prior period and determine the investment and data drivers.
steps.evidence: Variance analysis needs a better evidence and narrative workflow before automation.

steps.name: Review client report
steps.description: Review the draft report for accuracy, fair presentation, client context, and appropriate commentary before release.
steps.evidence: Final communication judgment and accountability remain human responsibilities.

steps.name: Import cash records
steps.description: Import bank, custodian, and internal ledger cash balances for each account and currency.
steps.evidence: High-volume structured ingestion with predictable inputs.

steps.name: Match balances and movements
steps.description: Match balances and cash movements across bank, custodian, and internal records and identify breaks.
steps.evidence: Deterministic matching is auditable and suitable for exception queues.

steps.name: Investigate reconciliation break
steps.description: Trace an unexplained difference to a settlement, fee, FX, timing, or booking issue and gather supporting evidence.
steps.evidence: Exception categories and source ownership should be standardized first.

steps.name: Approve adjustment
steps.description: Approve a correcting journal or escalation after reviewing evidence and segregation-of-duty requirements.
steps.evidence: Financial control approval requires accountable human review.

steps.name: Capture event notice
steps.description: Capture a corporate action notice, key dates, eligible holdings, and available election options from the custodian.
steps.evidence: Notice normalization and deadline controls vary by issuer and need stronger process design.

steps.name: Determine portfolio eligibility
steps.description: Determine affected portfolios and positions using record-date holdings and account restrictions.
steps.evidence: Eligibility is structured when holdings and terms are reliable.

steps.name: Choose election
steps.description: Choose among cash, stock, tender, or other options based on mandate, portfolio strategy, tax, and client instructions.
steps.evidence: The election is a material investment and client-specific decision.

steps.name: Submit and confirm election
steps.description: Submit the approved election before the deadline and confirm acceptance and settlement with the custodian.
steps.evidence: Controlled submission and confirmation are repeatable after approval.

steps.name: Read mandate language
steps.description: Review the signed investment management agreement and identify restrictions, thresholds, exceptions, and effective dates.
steps.evidence: Legal and client-specific interpretation is highly contextual.

steps.name: Translate restriction to rule
steps.description: Translate mandate language into a proposed machine-checkable rule with data requirements and tolerance handling.
steps.evidence: The process needs joint legal, investment, and data design rather than direct automation.

steps.name: Test rule against history
steps.description: Run the proposed rule against representative historical positions and investigate false positives and false negatives.
steps.evidence: Testing is repeatable but requires redesigned evidence and exception governance.

steps.name: Approve rule deployment
steps.description: Approve the coded restriction, version it, assign an owner, and release it into production monitoring.
steps.evidence: Control ownership and authorization must remain explicit and human.

steps.name: Load fee terms
steps.description: Load the applicable fee schedule, hurdle, high-water mark, crystallization date, and client-specific terms.
steps.evidence: Terms and effective-date data need stronger governance before automation.

steps.name: Calculate provisional fee
steps.description: Calculate the provisional performance fee using approved valuation, return, benchmark, and high-water-mark inputs.
steps.evidence: Once terms are controlled, the calculation is repeatable and testable.

steps.name: Review unusual result
steps.description: Investigate an unexpected fee result caused by flows, series, side pockets, valuation changes, or amended terms.
steps.evidence: Exception handling and valuation evidence need a consistent workflow.

steps.name: Approve fee invoice
steps.description: Review the final fee calculation and approve the invoice or client statement for release.
steps.evidence: Financial and client-impacting approval requires human accountability.

steps.name: Identify reviews due
steps.description: Identify clients whose periodic AML, KYC, sanctions, or beneficial-ownership review is due.
steps.evidence: Due-date identification is structured and should be consistently monitored.

steps.name: Request updated documents
steps.description: Request current identity, ownership, source-of-wealth, and tax-residency documentation from the client or intermediary.
steps.evidence: Standardized outreach and completeness tracking are suitable for controlled automation.

steps.name: Assess risk and discrepancies
steps.description: Assess updated information, investigate discrepancies, and determine whether enhanced due diligence is required.
steps.evidence: Regulated risk judgment and escalation should remain with compliance professionals.

steps.name: Record review outcome
steps.description: Record the review outcome, evidence, risk rating, restrictions, and next-review date in the client record.
steps.evidence: Structured record updates are repeatable with authorization and audit logging.

steps.name: Detect drift
steps.description: Compare current portfolio weights with targets, bands, cash needs, and approved investment restrictions.
steps.evidence: Drift detection is structured and can produce a transparent exception list.

steps.name: Generate trade proposal
steps.description: Generate candidate trades that address drift while considering liquidity, tax, transaction costs, and restrictions.
steps.evidence: Optimization inputs and approval boundaries need redesign before agentic proposals.

steps.name: Review investment rationale
steps.description: Review the candidate trades and decide whether they fit the portfolio objective, market view, client context, and current risks.
steps.evidence: Investment judgment and client context remain central.

steps.name: Approve rebalance
steps.description: Approve the final rebalance, document rationale, and release authorized orders for execution.
steps.evidence: Material trading authorization requires accountable human approval.

steps.name: Load liquidity data
steps.description: Load positions, market volumes, redemption assumptions, cash balances, and security liquidity classifications.
steps.evidence: Recurring structured data assembly is suitable with data-quality checks.

steps.name: Run stress scenarios
steps.description: Run approved redemption, market-volume, spread, and settlement scenarios across portfolios and funds.
steps.evidence: Scenario execution is repeatable when assumptions are versioned.

steps.name: Interpret liquidity result
steps.description: Interpret stressed cash needs, gates, liquidation horizons, and investor impacts under the scenario results.
steps.evidence: Forward-looking risk interpretation requires senior judgment.

steps.name: Recommend mitigation
steps.description: Recommend cash buffers, dealing restrictions, asset sales, or client communication based on the stress findings.
steps.evidence: Mitigation choices are consequential and context-dependent.

steps.name: Load report data
steps.description: Load positions, returns, benchmarks, fees, exposures, and client metadata into the reporting dataset.
steps.evidence: Scheduled structured ingestion is highly repeatable.

steps.name: Run validation rules
steps.description: Run completeness, reconciliation, period, sign, decimal, and benchmark validation rules against the report dataset.
steps.evidence: Rule-based validation is transparent and auditable.

steps.name: Resolve data exception
steps.description: Investigate a validation exception with the data owner and determine whether to correct, suppress, or escalate it.
steps.evidence: Ownership and exception policy should be standardized before automation.

steps.name: Certify report data
steps.description: Certify that report data is complete and accurate enough for client distribution and retain the evidence.
steps.evidence: Certification is an accountable control decision.

steps.name: Receive NAV package
steps.description: Receive the administrator's NAV package, valuation files, holdings, cash, and exception reports.
steps.evidence: Package intake and completeness checks are structured.

steps.name: Compare valuation movements
steps.description: Compare valuation movements, prices, FX, corporate actions, expenses, and unit changes against expected tolerances.
steps.evidence: Repeatable tolerances can identify a transparent exception queue.

steps.name: Assess materiality
steps.description: Assess whether a NAV exception is material, requires correction, affects investors, or can be accepted with documentation.
steps.evidence: Materiality and investor impact require accountable judgment.

steps.name: Approve NAV release
steps.description: Approve release of the NAV or require correction and investor-impact analysis before publication.
steps.evidence: Final release is a high-consequence control decision.

steps.name: Collect execution data
steps.description: Collect orders, fills, venues, timestamps, prices, benchmarks, liquidity, and broker information for the review period.
steps.evidence: Structured high-volume data collection is suitable with lineage controls.

steps.name: Run execution analytics
steps.description: Run transaction-cost, price, venue, timing, and outlier analytics against approved best-execution benchmarks.
steps.evidence: Analytics are repeatable when benchmarks and data definitions are governed.

steps.name: Investigate outlier
steps.description: Investigate an execution outlier using market conditions, order instructions, liquidity, broker rationale, and client restrictions.
steps.evidence: Evidence assembly and investigation workflow need stronger standardization.

steps.name: Conclude surveillance review
steps.description: Conclude whether execution quality and broker arrangements remain appropriate and record any escalation or remediation.
steps.evidence: Regulatory conclusion and remediation judgment should remain human-led.
